subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw define and support a runtime-neutral agent-core protocol for no-Node embedded or WASM ports, or should those ports remain independent external projects without a core compatibility contract?
rationale: Current source and docs show an intentionally Node-hosted TypeScript/Gateway runtime; choosing a portable ABI would affect runtime ownership, plugin SDK boundaries, Gateway protocol, storage/session semantics, providers, tools, and security policy.

options.title: Keep As Runtime-Portability RFC
options.body: Use this issue to design minimal schemas, conformance tests, and ownership boundaries before accepting embedded or WASM implementation work.

options.title: Scope To Plugin SDK Only
options.body: Route near-term language/runtime work through JSON-RPC plugin or harness APIs and leave full no-Node ports outside the supported OpenClaw contract.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: Decide that OpenClaw remains Node-hosted and external projects such as MimiClaw are independent ports without compatibility promises.

recommendation.title: Keep As Runtime-Portability RFC
recommendation.body: Use this issue to design minimal schemas, conformance tests, and ownership boundaries before accepting embedded or WASM implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already participated in the source-grounded keep-open discussion and is the best available routing owner for the runtime/platform direction choice.
